title:
Your CPF wants
its *money back*
source: source: CPF Board rules on accrued interest (2.5% p.a.)
caption:
You sell your HDB for $800,000. But far less cash lands in your bank. 🏦

Every CPF dollar you used goes back to your CPF, plus 2.5% a year compounded. Used $300K 15 years ago? That's about $435K back to CPF, a $135K difference in your cash proceeds.

Cash or CPF to service your mortgage? Comment CASH or CPF 👇

lines.say: You are selling your HDB for eight hundred thousand dollars. But far less cash lands in your bank.
lines.cap: you sell your HDB for $800K. but *far less cash* lands in your bank

lines.say: Every CPF dollar used for your home goes back to your CPF.
lines.cap: every CPF dollar used for your home *goes back to your CPF*

Used three hundred thousand upfront, fifteen years ago? You refund about four hundred and thirty five thousand.

lines.say: That's a one hundred and thirty five thousand dollar difference in your cash proceeds.
lines.cap: that's a *$135K difference* in your cash proceeds

lines.say: So plan your next home on cash proceeds. Not the sale price.
lines.cap: so plan your next home on *cash proceeds*, not sale price
